_comment: Text of the biomarker report made at the hospital (biomarkers/ncbio/report.py, M15). {placeholders} are filled by the report. Never put patient names here.
title: Finger Tapping
decisionSupport: Decision support for the clinician. Not a diagnosis.
demoBanner: Synthetic demo: made-up tapping, not a patient. It shows how a report looks and how each number is worked out.

summary.title: Results
summary.asymHint: Asymmetry = |R − L| ÷ (R + L). 0 means both hands are the same; 1 means one hand did not move.

step1.title: Points found in the video
step1.body: MediaPipe finds the thumb tip (point 4) and the index tip (point 8) of each hand, and the elbows and wrists of the body, in every frame.
step1.forearm: Forearm length, {hand}: the middle value (median) of the elbow-to-wrist distance over {n} frames = {px} px

step2.title: The tapping signal
step2.formula: d(t) = distance from thumb tip to index tip ÷ forearm length
step2.pre: Gaps up to {gap} s are filled in. Then a median filter over {median} frames and a Savitzky–Golay filter over {sg} frames ({sgs} s, order {order}) smooth out the jitter of the points.

oneTap.title: How one tap is measured
oneTap.body: Tap {n} of the {hand}, from {t0} s to {t1} s.

step3.title: Taps
step3.body: A tap runs from one closing of the fingers to the next. A closing counts when the dip is at least {prom} % of the signal's range and at least {gap} s after the one before.

perTap.amplitude: each tap: highest d − lowest d
perTap.period: each tap: time of the next closing − time of this closing
perTap.speed: each tap: largest |d′| (change of d per second)
perTap.acceleration: each tap: largest |d″| (change of d′ per second)

footer.sources: Formulas: DNE toolbox (IEEE JBHI 2024, Table A-II) and Hoang et al. 2022 (arXiv 2205.07209). Distances are in forearm lengths, so the distance to the camera does not change them.
footer.privacy: Computed at the hospital. This file holds no name or record number.

overlay._comment: Drawn on video frames by OpenCV: plain ASCII only.
overlay.legend: R = patient's right hand, L = patient's left hand
